prompt: A luxury watch brand is setting the price for a new limited-edition model. The candidate's framework: (1) The cost of the brand's office lease; (2) What collectors would pay for scarcity; (3) Prices of comparable limited editions; (4) Production cost of the model. What is the flaw in this framework?

options.text: Buckets 2 and 3 overlap: comparable editions set what collectors pay
options.feedback: Comparables inform willingness to pay, but what collectors would pay and what similar editions sold for are separate inputs.

options.text: Missing: what the movement and materials cost
options.feedback: Movement and materials are the production cost, which bucket 4 covers.

options.text: Bucket 1 doesn't belong: office rent has no link to this price
options.feedback: Right. Office rent is overhead with no link to this price. Replace it with the effect on the brand: the price must protect its luxury positioning.

options.text: It's a generic cost-plus approach: luxury prices aren't set from cost
options.feedback: The framework starts from collectors and comparables, with cost as one input. It isn't cost-plus. The flaw is bucket 1.

explanation: Luxury pricing balances collector value, comparables, cost and brand positioning. Office rent is overhead with no link to this price.

extras.corrected_framework: Collector willingness to pay; comparable editions; production cost; brand positioning
